status: authored 2026-10-09; tools/route4_events.py builds the sites and writes the scene, quest, dialogue, progression and reward records below into their shared files; NOT run in a world
note: Route 4's middle (walked 1085-2263 of 3,453 blocks, cells B3-B4, band 3, cap 35): four events and one find, west to east, because the leg had six trainers and nothing else. One quest, evt_route4_thaw_road, carries the whole chain (a quest may read only its own fields: tools/validate_data.py quest-dialogue), so the finale can greet a player by what they did at the earlier sites. The story: a packer's lead mule bolts at a rockfall on the cirque headwall (1), leaves tracks at a steaming hollow on the trough floor (2) and a dragged crate under the east wall (the find), and walks the old summit road, a line of numbered stones that count down to a summit that is not there (3), to the Displaced City's gate, where warm air and cherry petals come out of the hill into the snow (4). Every event stands alone and pays alone; the finale reads the others' flags only to change who greets the player, so no order is forced and no player is locked out of anything by the order they walk.
design_rules: no new money: every reward is an item, none of them in the Bank's buy list (data/bank.json buys), so the income model (data/markets.json income_basis) is untouched; cash 0 per hour
no progression item: the only held item is Never-Melt Ice, which the wild pools already carry (data/spawns.json); no Exp. Candy, IV candy, Rare Candy, Lucky Egg, stone or TM
one claim per player per reward (grant_reward_once with a claim field; the find is an advancement)
each event is complete without the others; the finale's four opening lines differ by who has done what and its reward does not

quest.lore_rule: Hallam's accident is a work accident on a freight route, not the Worldshift or the Haven Compact; the stones and the gate are the Displaced City's own (data/placements.json displaced_city plan: 'the old road climbs the ridge to the top of the mountain'; data/towns.json displaced_city entrance 'a meltwater cave mouth on the trough flank'); the warm-air hook is docs/story/SIDEQUESTS.md SQ-G5-02

objectives.text: Hallam's string bolted at the headwall: read the lip and the post, and tell her which way her mule went.
Read the prints, the pool and the petal on the trough floor, then follow the prints east.
Walk the old summit road down its numbered stones and read the last one.
Find the grey mule at the thaw gate, and the keeper.

reward_packer.why: a packer's thanks: four Oran Berries, growable by anyone; the reward ladder on this leg starts small

reward_gate.why: the payoff: a held item for the cold, a cutting from the grove under the hill (plantable anywhere a sapling grows) and three Sitrus Berries; no cash, nothing the Bank buys, nothing that advances a gate

headwall_camp.title: Headwall camp: the string that bolted

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: Don't come down the headwall at a run. The whole face let go in the night.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: It took my string with it, near enough. Biscuit, my lead mule, snapped his rope and went. A Gogoat, grey, bad manners.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Fresh stone across the lip. Hoofprints on the bare shelf, going the wrong way for a mule that wanted to stay.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: Look at the lip and the post. Then tell me which way he went. I can't leave the loads.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: Well? You've seen the lip and the post. Which way did he go?

responses.text: East, down off the shelf. He pulled free and ran with the slide.
Back the way you came, up the mountain.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: Up? Into the rock that's still coming down? He's stubborn, not stupid. Look at the lead again.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: Don't say that where I can hear it. The prints go along the shelf, not off it. Look again.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: East. Of course, east. The ground goes warm that way, and he can smell it.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: There is one place on this trough where the snow won't lie: an old stone gate on the south-west flank, and a wind out of the hill like a bakery's. If he's anywhere, he's there. Take these for the looking.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: And if you find him, he bites. Don't take it personally.

nodes.speaker: hallam
nodes.text: Still here with the loads. Still not taking it personally.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Scree across the lip, still bright where it split. It fell east, with the slope, and the shelf above it is bare to the rock. Whatever stood here was carried that way.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Loose stone, newly fallen.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A hitching post with a stub of rope on it. The rope isn't chewed: it parted under strain, and the strands all point east, the way something heavy pulled.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A hitching post.

steam_hollow.title: Steam hollow: where the snow won't lie

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Cloven prints, wide-set, driven deep: a heavy animal moving fast, then slowing. They come in from the road and stop at the ring of bare moss. Others go out again, east, toward the wall.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Hoofprints.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Open water in the middle of a frozen floor, and warm: the steam comes up in a column and the moss round it is green. Snow lands on the ring and goes. Nothing feeds it from above.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A pool.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A pink petal, whole, on the moss. The nearest cherry tree you know of is a very long way from here, and it is winter. A red pennant stands up against the east wall, a long walk off.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: The prints run east across the road to a red pennant at the foot of the wall. The petal is pink and soft and very out of place.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A pink petal on green moss, in the snow. Look around the hollow first.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A petal.

summit_road.title: The old summit road: five stones to a summit that is not there

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A 0, and SUMMIT. Under it, cut smaller and later, by a different hand: THE SUMMIT IS BELOW. ASK AT THE GATE.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: SUMMIT, 0. THE SUMMIT IS BELOW. ASK AT THE GATE.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: A stone with a 0 on it. You did not climb for it, and it is not a summit. Walk the road from the first stone.

effects.text: Old Summit Road: five stones to the top.
Four stones. The wind has turned warm.
Three stones. There is no climb.
Two stones. Something smells of blossom.
Summit. There is no mountain here. Read the stone.

thaw_gate.title: The thaw gate: the summit is below

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: You read the stones and you have Hallam's look about you. Both of you walk in like it's your gate. Good. Slowly, though: look at the snow.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: Hallam sends someone every time. Slowly, now: look at the snow, not at me.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: You came by the road, and you read the last stone. Slowly, now: look at the snow, not at me.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: Mind the ground. Slowly, now: look at the snow, not at me.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Warm wind is coming out of the hill. It carries cherry petals, pink on white, a long way from any tree, and where they land the snow has gone to moss. Somewhere in the drift a grey animal is pretending to be a rock.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: Well. What brings you to the top of nothing?

responses.text: The stones on the road. They counted down.
Where does the warm wind come from?
A grey Gogoat. He bites, I'm told.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: They are right. They were laid when this was a summit town, and they count what a road to a summit counts. The mountain isn't here now; the count didn't change. Ask me something else.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: Up the way behind me, from the city. We call it spring and don't say how long it has been spring. Ask me something else.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: Biscuit. Yes. He came up the road two nights ago, ate a lantern wick, and has been sulking in the petals since. Hallam can have him back, or he can stay, whichever he allows.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: Take these. A cutting from the grove down there, which will grow wherever you plant it and which the grove will not miss; something for the cold; and berries, because the Gogoat will want them off you.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: The way down behind me is lit all the way. There's a waystone at the bottom of it, and it'll know you for next time. We have no Centre. We have a kettle.

nodes.speaker: oriel
nodes.text: The way down is lit. Mind the petals; they're slippery.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Biscuit looks at you. Then at your pockets. Then at the lantern wick he is chewing, with total contempt.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Biscuit has decided you are his. He will not be told otherwise, and he is standing on your foot.

nodes.speaker: narration
nodes.text: Cherry petals, drifted against the stones. They are soft and wet and warm, a day's walk from the nearest cherry tree you know of.

actors.name: Biscuit
actors.not_yours: That Gogoat is sulking at somebody else.

find.place: the east wall's foot, 104 blocks off Route 4, under a red pennant
find.message: Dragged here and abandoned, one strap still tied: a packer's spare stores. Two Sitrus Berries and two Pecha Berries, dry under the oilcloth.
find.why: the second step of the chain's reward ladder (berries 4, then 4 here, then the gate's three, a held item and a sapling); the tracks from the hollow lead here and a red pennant shows it from the road
